items.title: Cascadu interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, November 15, 2019
items.q: And I’m sitting there with the guy. I don’t know him, I don’t know anything about him, I just know that I saw you in my dream, you’re the one, don’t move, don’t say a word.

ctx.x: I mean, well, I want to talk about you and your band mates, the thing you did yesterday was — when I asked a question I said, “My head is spinning.” And it was really true. Because there’s something about, this is not a question but rather an observation and maybe you can talk about it. There’s something about this percussion rhythms and things that you gentlemen played that reaches so deep into you — I don’t know what it is, but — like if you were in New York City and you were walking and all of a sudden you…

I think the drum has the ability to reach deeply into your soul. That’s the power of that vibrating membrane and that piece of wood. It has the power to call you. And there’s something spiritually that we respond to, that people respond to, just like you’re saying you know. You hear these drums and there’s something that you want to go and visit it. You want to be in the presence of that. And I think it’s a very primal call to the deepest part of our being. Because we’re all connected to that somehow or the other…

that place where we come from. Monk, I’ve seen, in Trinidad, there are people, and we have a very, very strong drum culture in Trinidad. And I have been to concerts in these big halls, You know people come in all — their suits, all suited up, and we come, we are a British colony for over 150 years, a Spanish colony for over 300 years etcetera. You know? And you know people will speak and dress in a very European way. And that drum would play in that concert hall. And people would start to, you know, dressed up in…
